item.title: 2nd Friday ArtAbout reception: Christine Shackel — Fri Oct 9, 6:00 PM — Logos Books
item.description: World’s Edge Christine Shackel watercolor and ink October 6 to 31 2nd Friday ArtAbout Reception: October 9, 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. Logos Books, 513 Second Street, Davis, CA, 95616 Christine attended Holy Names University in Oakland where she received her B.A in Art and Philosophy. The following year she earned a teaching credential in art education. Currently, she is semi-retired and belongs to a group of enthusiastic local painters. Artist’s Statement “World’s Edge” is created with the broad concepts of chaos and order. The watercolor medium lends itself to chaos when you let the paint “paint itself”. By using wet and dry surfaces and dropping paint randomly onto them, the result is an uncontrolled reaction of pigment and capillary action. The “control” part comes when I try to make something out of what has happened on the paper. My overall sense is that the paintings look very cosmic. item.title: Savor: Fresh Starts: How California Farmers Markets Changed the Way We Eat — Wed Oct 28, 5:00 PM — Robert Mondavi Institute - Sensory Building
item.description:
Join us for this quarter's Savor event: Fresh Starts: How California Farmers Markets Changed the Way We Eat.
The formation of the Davis Farmers Market 50 years ago was a revolutionary movement to connect consumers directly to farmers and helped shape the fresh flavors of California cuisine. Markets have been a cornerstone of the community and have also played a pivotal role in food access, especially during supply chain shortages and widespread food recalls. Inevitably, markets have evolved. Join us as we explore the history, impact and changing role of farmers markets in local communities.
The event will feature a panel of leading industry experts including:
Ann Evans, UC Davis alumna, co-founder of the Davis Farmers Market and Davis Food Co-op, author and former mayor and city council member of the City of DavisSam Greenlee, chief executive officer of Alchemist Community Development CorporationChutharat Sae Tong, co-owner of Majka Pizzeria and Bakery in SacramentoModerator Ca

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Oct 28, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants

Stop by to shop for fresh, locally grown produce, artisan goods, prepared foods and other market favorites from local farmers and vendors. It’s a great opportunity to stock up for the week, meet up with friends, support local growers and food makers, and enjoy a beautiful afternoon in Central Park. The Davis Farmers Market is celebrating its 50th Anniversary in 2026, marking five decades of bringing fresh food, local farmers and the Davis community together. Wednesday Market Details:

item.title: Davis City Council Meetings — Thu Dec 17, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis City Council provides policy direction, establishes goals, and sets priorities for City government. City Council holds regular meetings beginning at 6:30 p.m. on Tuesdays. Most commonly, meetings are held on the first and third Tuesdays of the month, with additional meetings scheduled as needed. The City Council meeting schedule is subject to change.
The Davis City Council meets in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. All regular meeting materials are posted at least 72 hours in advance and special meeting materials at least 24 hours in advance.
Visit the City Council site for information on agenda, special meetings, and more.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Human Relations Commission Meetings — Thu Dec 24, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis Human Relations Commission (HRC) meetings aim to promote mutual respect, understanding, justice, and advancing the human rights of all people. The Human Relations Commission meets on the fourth Thursday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Commission takes a recess in July (no meeting in July).
Meetings take place in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. For more information on meetings, membership, resolutions, and more, visit the Human Relations Commission site.
The HRC makes recommendations around equity and discrimination in the City, and supports the City in preventing and addressing discrimination while promoting diversity, equality, and justice relevant to the goals and policies of the City Council.
To contact or send emails to the commission, email: HRC@cityofdavis.org
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Danilo Campos: Out and About — Fri Oct 9 — Pence Gallery
item.description:
Danilo Campos: Out and About Exhibit: October 9 – November 29, 2026 Reception: Friday, October 9, 2026 (Free) Danilo Campos is a Sacramento-based artist whose recent series of paintings explore his love of new places and experiences. His antidote to everyday routines is to go out and wander, whether it’s a new neighborhood, a new place, or campsite. His current series of work reflects his way of seeming to mindlessly go ‘out and about,’ but coming back with gems of resources. This exhibit is sponsored by Kim Ohlson & Allen Barnes. Image: Danilo Campos, “Sheltered Cove”
Source: The Dirt

item.title: portraits of things: Paintings by Gioia Fonda and Charlie Gill — Fri Oct 9 — Pence Gallery
item.description: portraits of things: Paintings by Gioia Fonda and Charlie Gill Exhibit: October 9 – November 29, 2026 Reception: Friday, October 9, 6-9 PM (Free) Artist Talk: Sunday, November 8, 2-3:30 PM (Free) Interdisciplinary artist Gioia Fonda has long collected colorful toys, both for their intrinsic charm and as creative inspiration. As a student at California College of the Arts, she arranged small collectibles into still-life compositions, captured them on film, and processed the photos at a local drugstore. Captivated by these arrangements, her advisor, Charlie Gill, painted spare compositions based on her photographs—works that now hang alongside hers. For this exhibition, Fonda has created a series of new paintings featuring similar arrangements of toys and found objects. She is also offering an opportunity for members of the public to exhibit their own small works on paper, riffing on some of her recent photos. Artists may add to this display throughout the duration of the show. Sponsor

item.title: Davis Waldorf School's Parent & Child Class — Fri Oct 9, 10:00 AM — Davis Waldorf School
item.description:
The first three years in a child’s life are an amazing time of growth that fill parents and caregivers with awe and wonder. Parent & Child classes are held in a warm and welcoming environment that is carefully arranged for creative play in our Buttercup Preschool room. This program offers the very young child freedom to explore within loving boundaries, and teaches parents/caregivers about Waldorf education’s many benefits. Classes are led by an experienced Early Childhood educator and echo the rhythms of the Waldorf preschool. Additionally, classes offer caregivers a place to connect about child development and parenting techniques. We welcome caregivers of all kinds—parents, grandparents, nannies—to join our sessions!
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Fri Oct 9, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Birds & Bikes — Fri Oct 9, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: Axis Gallery is proud to announce Birds & Bikes, a collaborative art exhibition bringing together regional artists to explore the poetic intersections of avian flight and human motion. Running from October 2 through November 1, 2026, the exhibition showcases a dynamic range of works from intricate metal sculptures and imaginative textile art to curated gallery shop goods, celebrating the beauty of migration alongside the engineering of daily travel. The exhibition features a direct partnership with the City of Sacramento Office of Arts and Culture (OAC) Art in Public Places program and North Natomas Jibe. Birds & Bikes serves as an artistic tie-in to the upcoming Birds and Benches project, which will install artist-designed public benches across North Natomas Regional Park. Mehregan مهرگان or Jashn-e Mehr جشن مهر is a Zoroastrian and Persian festival celebrated to honor the Yazata Mithra,, which is responsible for friendship, affection and love. Under the Sasanian Empire (224–651), Mehregan was the second most important festival, falling behind Nowruz.

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Dec 16, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

item.title: Día de los Muertos Doll Making Workshop (Davis) — Sun Nov 1, 2:00 PM — Blanchard Room
item.description:
We invite children ages 8 through 14 to join artist Ramona García for a Día de los Muertos doll-making workshop. Participants will be making and decorating traditional Mexican Lupita dolls. Ramona García will share the history of the Lupita doll as a beloved folk toy from Central Mexico and will guide the participants through the process of doll-making. Registration is required. The workshop is limited to 20 participants. Parents may accompany their children and help them during the workshop but materials will be provided for the children only.
You can register here or at the Children's Desk in person.
